description.en: Arab traders who controlled incense and spice routes across what is now Jordan and the Negev from Petra, a capital cut into sandstone cliffs. They stored water in hidden cisterns, wrote in a script derived from Aramaic, and lost their kingdom to Rome in 106 CE.
description.es: Comerciantes árabes que controlaron las rutas del incienso y las especias por la actual Jordania y el Néguev desde Petra, una capital tallada en acantilados de arenisca. Almacenaban agua en cisternas ocultas, escribían con una escritura derivada del arameo y perdieron su reino ante Roma en 106 e. c.
description.zh: 阿拉伯商人，以开凿于砂岩峭壁中的都城佩特拉为中心，控制着穿越今约旦和内盖夫的香料与乳香商路。他们把水储存在隐蔽的蓄水池里，使用源自阿拉姆文的文字，公元106年王国被罗马吞并。

sources.citation: Brown University Petra Great Temple excavations (2017), Volume III, via PeriodO: "Nabatean period" (312 BC – AD 106).
The New Encyclopedia of Archaeological Excavations in the Holy Land (1993), vol. 4, via PeriodO: "Nabatean kingdom" (168 BCE – 106 CE).

World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Nabatea" (a Greek expedition against the Nabataeans in 312 BCE; kingdom dated from 168 BCE, the first known king, to annexation by Rome under Trajan in 106 CE).

note.en: The bar starts at the first certain written mention of the Nabataeans (312 BCE) and turns solid at 168 BCE, the date of the oldest known Nabataean inscription, which names a king.
note.es: La barra comienza con la primera mención escrita segura de los nabateos (312 a. e. c.) y se vuelve sólida en 168 a. e. c., fecha de la inscripción nabatea más antigua conocida, que nombra a un rey.
note.zh: 这条横栏从纳巴泰人的首次确凿文字记载（公元前312年）开始，到公元前168年变为实线，这是已知最古老的纳巴泰铭文的年代，铭文提到了一位国王。

sources.citation: Erickson-Gini, Tali (2010). Nabataean Settlement and Self-Organized Economy in the Central Negev, via PeriodO: "Early Nabataean" (ca. 168 – 85 BCE).
Erickson-Gini, Tali (2010). Nabataean Settlement and Self-Organized Economy in the Central Negev, via PeriodO: "Middle Nabataean" (85 BCE – 70 CE).
Erickson-Gini, Tali (2010). Nabataean Settlement and Self-Organized Economy in the Central Negev, via PeriodO: "Late Nabataean" (70 – 106 CE).

title.en: Antigonus I sends troops against the Nabataeans at a rock refuge, the first certain mention of them in writing
title.es: Antígono I envía tropas contra los nabateos en un refugio rocoso, la primera mención escrita segura de ellos
title.zh: 安提柯一世派兵攻打纳巴泰人的岩石避难所，这是他们最早的确凿文字记载

sources.citation: Livius.org, "Diodorus on the Nabataeans" (Diodorus 19.94–100, drawing on Hieronymus of Cardia).

World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Nabatea" (a Greek expedition against the Nabataeans in 312 BCE; kingdom dated from 168 BCE, the first known king, to annexation by Rome under Trajan in 106 CE).
Wikipedia, "Nabataeans" (first mention 312/311 BC).

note.en: Diodorus describes an attack on 'a certain rock'. Some scholars identify it with Petra, others with Sela (Es-Sela).
note.es: Diodoro describe un ataque a 'cierta roca'. Algunos especialistas la identifican con Petra, otros con Sela (Es-Sela).
note.zh: 狄奥多罗斯描述了对“一块岩石”的进攻。有学者认为这块岩石是佩特拉，也有人认为是塞拉（埃斯-塞拉）。

title.en: Aretas I becomes the first Nabataean king named in surviving sources, in an inscription at Halutza and in 2 Maccabees
title.es: Aretas I es el primer rey nabateo nombrado en las fuentes conservadas, en una inscripción de Halutza y en 2 Macabeos
title.zh: 阿雷塔斯一世成为现存资料中最早被提及的纳巴泰国王，见于哈卢扎的铭文和《玛加伯下》

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Aretas I" (oldest Nabataean inscription, 168 BC, at Halutza; 2 Maccabees 5:8).

World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Nabatea" (a Greek expedition against the Nabataeans in 312 BCE; kingdom dated from 168 BCE, the first known king, to annexation by Rome under Trajan in 106 CE).
Nabataea.net, "History of Nabataea".
The New Encyclopedia of Archaeological Excavations in the Holy Land (1993), vol. 4, via PeriodO: "Nabatean kingdom" begins 168 BCE.

note.es: Las fuentes dan 169 o 168 a. e. c.
note.zh: 各资料给出的年份为公元前169年或168年。

title.en: Aretas III becomes ruler of Damascus as Seleucid power fails there, and has coins struck with his name in Greek
title.es: Aretas III pasa a gobernar Damasco cuando el poder seléucida se desmorona allí, y manda acuñar monedas con su nombre en griego
title.zh: 阿雷塔斯三世在塞琉古势力衰落之际成为大马士革的统治者，并铸造以希腊文刻其名的钱币

sources.citation: Nabataea.net, "History of Nabataea" (in 85 BC Aretas III occupied Damascus at the request of its citizens; coins with his image and his name in Greek).
Wikipedia, "Aretas III" (reigned 87–62 BCE; Damascus around 85 BCE).
Wikipedia, "Nabataeans" (lord of Damascus and Coele-Syria, 85 BC).

note.en: Accounts differ on how he gained Damascus: some say he occupied it at its citizens' request, others that he took it from the weakening Seleucids. The year, about 85 BCE, is not in dispute.
note.es: Los relatos difieren sobre cómo obtuvo Damasco: unos dicen que la ocupó a petición de sus ciudadanos, otros que se la arrebató a unos seléucidas cada vez más débiles. El año, hacia 85 a. e. c., no se discute.
note.zh: 关于他如何获得大马士革，说法不一：有的说他应该城居民之请而占领，有的说他从日渐衰弱的塞琉古人手中夺取了该城。年份约为公元前85年，这一点没有争议。

title.en: The Treasury (Al-Khazneh) is carved into the cliff at Petra, probably for King Aretas IV
title.es: El Tesoro (Al-Khazneh) se talla en el acantilado de Petra, probablemente para el rey Aretas IV
title.zh: 卡兹尼神殿（宝库）在佩特拉的峭壁上凿成，很可能是为阿雷塔斯四世国王所建

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Al-Khazneh" (mausoleum and crypt, early 1st century AD, reign of Aretas IV).
University of St Andrews news, "St Andrews researchers discover hidden tomb at Petra" (tomb walls dated mid 1st century BC to early 2nd century AD).

note.en: The facade has no dated inscription. It is usually placed in the late 1st century BCE or early 1st century CE and attributed to Aretas IV. Sediment analysis of a tomb beneath it gives a range from the mid 1st century BCE to the early 2nd century CE.
note.es: La fachada no tiene inscripción fechada. Suele situarse a finales del siglo I a. e. c. o a comienzos del siglo I e. c. y atribuirse a Aretas IV. El análisis de sedimentos de una tumba bajo ella da un margen que va de mediados del siglo I a. e. c. a comienzos del siglo II e. c.
note.zh: 这座立面上没有纪年铭文。通常认为它建于公元前1世纪末或公元1世纪初，属于阿雷塔斯四世。对其下一座墓室的沉积物检测给出的年代范围是公元前1世纪中叶至公元2世纪初。

title.en: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom under Trajan and makes it the province of Arabia
title.es: Roma anexiona el reino nabateo bajo Trajano y lo convierte en la provincia de Arabia
title.zh: 罗马在图拉真治下吞并纳巴泰王国，将其改为阿拉伯行省

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Nabatea" (a Greek expedition against the Nabataeans in 312 BCE; kingdom dated from 168 BCE, the first known king, to annexation by Rome under Trajan in 106 CE).
Nabataea.net, "History of Nabataea".
The New Encyclopedia of Archaeological Excavations in the Holy Land (1993), vol. 4, via PeriodO: "Nabatean kingdom" ends 106 CE.
Wikipedia, "Arabia Petraea" (annexation in 106 AD; Rabbel II died in 105).

note.en: Rabbel II died in early 105 CE. Sources date the annexation to 105 or 106 CE.
note.es: Rabel II murió a comienzos de 105 e. c. Las fuentes datan la anexión en 105 o 106 e. c.
note.zh: 拉贝尔二世于公元105年初去世。各资料将吞并定在公元105年或106年。

text.en: A Greek account of events in 312 BCE says the Nabataeans banned planting grain or building houses, and hid stucco-lined water cisterns in the desert.
text.es: Un relato griego de hechos del 312 a. e. c. dice que los nabateos prohibían sembrar cereales y construir casas, y escondían en el desierto cisternas de agua revestidas de estuco.
text.zh: 一份记述公元前312年事件的希腊史料称，纳巴泰人禁止种植谷物和建造房屋，并在沙漠中隐藏涂有灰泥的蓄水池。

sources.citation: Livius.org, "Diodorus on the Nabataeans" (Diodorus 19.94–100).

text.en: The Nabataean script, in use from the 2nd century BCE, developed into a cursive form from which the Arabic alphabet grew.
text.es: La escritura nabatea, en uso desde el siglo II a. e. c., desarrolló una forma cursiva de la que surgió el alfabeto árabe.
text.zh: 纳巴泰文字自公元前2世纪起使用，后来发展出一种草书体，阿拉伯字母即由此而来。

sources.citation: Omniglot, "Nabataean" (script developed from Aramaic in the 2nd century BC; the Arabic script grew from cursive Nabataean).
Wikipedia, "Nabataean alphabet".
